title_en: US Minerals and Metals Co., Ltd. v. Xiamen United Development (Group) Co., Ltd. — debt dispute
ruling_gist_en: An enterprise that has been registered and approved by the competent national authority as a legal person shall independently bear civil liability in accordance with the law. In determining whether the founding unit of such enterprise shall bear civil liability for the enterprise's debts, it is necessary to strictly examine the founding unit's capital contribution to the enterprise, and whether the founding unit has illegally withdrawn the enterprise's registered capital or maliciously transferred the enterprise's assets. If the founding unit has no fault in the above respects, it shall not bear joint and several liability for compensation for the enterprise's debts.

full_text_en:
U.S. Minerals and Metals Corporation v. Xiamen United Development (Group) Co., Ltd. — Debt Dispute

【Ruling Summary】

An enterprise with legal personality that has been approved and registered by the competent state authority shall, in accordance with the law, independently assume civil liability. In determining whether the founding entity of such an enterprise shall bear civil liability for the enterprise's debts, it must be strictly examined whether the founding entity has made its capital contributions to the enterprise, whether it has withdrawn the enterprise's registered capital, and whether it has maliciously transferred the enterprise's property. If the founding entity has no fault in the above aspects, it shall not bear joint and several compensation liability for the enterprise's debts.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 4

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): U.S. Minerals and Metals Corporation. Domicile: 120 Schor Road, Leonia, New Jersey, United States of America.

Legal Representative: Liu Daojing, President of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Li Zhiquan, Attorney at Beijing Beige Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yaoquan, Attorney at Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Xiamen United Development (Group) Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 31, Huli Avenue, Huli District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Wang Xianrong, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Xu, Attorney at Fujian Xiamen Xufeng Law Firm.

The appellant, U.S. Minerals and Metals Corporation (hereinafter referred to as U.S. Minerals), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2003) Min Jing Chu Zi No. 031 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) in the case of debt dispute with the respondent, Xiamen United Development (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiamen United Development). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Yun presiding as the presiding judge, and acting judges Chen Jizhong and Zhou Xiang participating in the deliberation, and conducted the trial. This case is now concluded.

Facts Found at First Instance:

On September 2, 1983, with the approval of the Fujian Provincial People's Government, Xiamen Special Economic Zone Construction and Development Company, the Trust and Consulting Company of the Head Office of the Bank of China, and five Hong Kong and Macao banks (Chiyu Banking Corporation Ltd. Hong Kong, Hua Chiao Commercial Bank Ltd. Hong Kong, Nanyang Commercial Bank Ltd. Hong Kong, Po Sang Bank Ltd. Hong Kong, and Nam Tung Investment Co., Ltd. Macau) jointly established Xiamen Special Economic Zone United Development Co., Ltd. The Fujian Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce registered it on October 18 of the same year, with the enterprise type being a Sino-foreign joint venture, registered capital of RMB 250 million, and the equity ratios among the three parties being: Xiamen Special Economic Zone Construction and Development Company 51%, Trust and Consulting Company of the Head Office of the Bank of China 34%, and the five Hong Kong and Macao banks 15%. On May 14, 1993, the former Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation (hereinafter referred to as the former MOFTEC) approved its name change to Xiamen United Development Co., Ltd. with approval certificate No. (1993) 119, and issued a Foreign Investment Enterprise Approval Certificate for the People's Republic of China. On May 22 of the same year, the State Administration for Industry and Commerce approved the name change registration.

On June 14, 1986, Xiamen Special Economic Zone United Development Co., Ltd. submitted an application report to the Xiamen Municipal Economic and Trade Commission of Fujian Province (hereinafter referred to as Xiamen Economic and Trade Commission) for the establishment of Xiamen United Development Import & Export Trade Company. The main content of the report was: "Since the approval of the establishment of Xiamen United Development Import & Export Trade Co., Ltd. by your Commission on October 30, 1984, with Document Xia Jingmao (1984) No. 097, the export earnings in 1985 reached USD 3.3 million, and business operations have been normal. Although the source of funds was allocated by United Development Company, there was no foreign equity participation. In order to clarify the relationship between Sino-foreign joint ventures and wholly state-owned enterprises, we hereby apply for the establishment of 'Xiamen United Development Import & Export Trade Company,' which shall be of a wholly state-owned nature, with independent accounting and self-financing..." On June 16 of the same year, Xiamen Economic and Trade Commission, with Document Xia Jingmao Shang (1986) No. 625, approved the establishment of "Xiamen United Development Import & Export Trade Company" as a wholly state-owned enterprise. On June 18 of the same year, it was registered with the Xiamen Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce and issued a business license. On August 10, 1992, the former MOFTEC approved Xiamen United Development Import & Export Trade Company to engage in import and export business within and outside the province. On August 31 of the same year, it obtained an import and export enterprise qualification certificate issued by the Ministry. On October 12, 1993, with the approval of the former MOFTEC, Xiamen United Development Import & Export Trade Company was renamed to Xiamen United Development (Group) Import & Export Trade Company (hereinafter referred to as United Development Trade Company). On December 13, 1998, the former MOFTEC revoked the import and export operation rights of United Development Trade Company with Document (1998) Wai Jing Mao Zheng Shen Han Zi No. 1792. On July 5, 2001, the Xiamen Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, on the ground of failure to participate in annual inspections as required, served a public notice of administrative penalty to United Development Trade Company, deciding to revoke its business license.

Further found: Between August and October 1992, U.S. Minerals entered into nine contracts with United Development Trade Company, under which U.S. Minerals sold 2,000 tons of aluminum ingots and 5,000 tons of electrolytic copper to United Development Trade Company. After receiving the goods, United Development Trade Company failed to pay the full purchase price in time as contracted. U.S. Minerals then applied for arbitration to the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission on October 6, 1994, in accordance with the arbitration clause in the contracts. On November 6, 1995, the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission rendered an award, ordering United Development Trade Company to repay USD 7,495,343.40 to U.S. Minerals before January 30, 1996, with overdue interest calculated at an annual rate of 8%. After the award became effective, U.S. Minerals immediately applied to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province for enforcement. Due to the serious operating losses of the judgment debtor and lack of property available for enforcement, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court ruled on November 23, 1998 to suspend enforcement.

On November 7, 2003, U.S. Minerals filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting that Xiamen United Development bear joint and several liability for the debt of USD 7,495,343.40 owed by United Development Trade Company, plus interest calculated at an annual rate of 8% from February 1, 1992 to the date of actual payment.

The court of first instance held that: The main issue in this case concerns whether Xiamen United Development is a proper subject for assuming the debt. Since Xiamen United Development is a domestic legal person in China and both parties have not chosen to apply foreign law, the law of the People's Republic of China shall apply as the governing law for resolving this dispute.

Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, a limited liability company is an enterprise legal person, and an enterprise legal person is an organization that has civil capacity for rights and civil capacity for conduct, independently enjoying civil rights and assuming civil obligations in accordance with the law. Therefore, whether the defendant in this case is a proper party and whether it should bear joint and several compensation liability for the debt owed by United Development Trade Company to the plaintiff depends on whether United Development Trade Company has the qualification of an enterprise legal person. According to the records of the Xiamen Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, on June 16, 1986, upon the application of the defendant, the Xiamen Economic and Trade Commission approved the establishment of United Development Trade Company to engage in import and export business. On June 18 of the same year, it was registered with the Xiamen Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce as an enterprise of a wholly state-owned nature, with independent accounting and self-financing, and was issued a business license for an enterprise legal person. Subsequently, the former MOFTEC approved the company to engage in import and export business within and outside the province in August 1992, and issued an import and export enterprise qualification certificate. Therefore, based on the industrial and commercial enterprise file materials, when United Development Trade Company engaged in international trade transactions with the plaintiff, it had been approved and registered by the relevant state authorities, obtained the qualification of an enterprise legal person, and should independently assume civil liability to the outside world in accordance with the law. As to whether the defendant, as a Sino-foreign joint venture, could apply to establish a wholly state-owned import and export company (United Development Trade Company) under the laws and regulations at that time, the plaintiff argued that the defendant was a joint venture and could not establish a wholly state-owned import and export enterprise, and that the defendant had deceived the competent authorities by fraudulent means to obtain the approval documents, making the establishment illegal, and the court should not recognize its legal personality. The defendant argued that although it was registered as a Sino-foreign joint venture, because the foreign investment ratio did not reach the statutory 25% and was in foreign exchange, and all shareholders were actually Chinese entities, the competent authorities only treated it as a joint venture enjoying joint venture treatment, but it was not essentially a joint venture. Therefore, the competent authorities' characterization of United Development Trade Company as a wholly state-owned enterprise was legal and in line with the national policy at the time. Moreover, the nature of the enterprise did not affect the way the enterprise legal person assumed responsibility. In this regard, the court of first instance held that: The determination of the enterprise nature of the defendant and whether the defendant could establish United Development Trade Company under the laws and policies at that time should be approved and determined by the relevant competent administrative authorities in accordance with the laws and policies at that time. If the plaintiff had objections to the administrative act of the competent authorities in approving the establishment of United Development Trade Company at that time, it could seek resolution through separate administrative litigation procedures. In this case, there was no evidence showing that the defendant, as Xiamen United Development Company, concealed the true situation or deceived the competent authorities in the process of applying for the establishment of United Development Trade Company, nor was there any situation such as insufficient registered capital or subsequent withdrawal of capital that would allow the denial of its corporate personality. Therefore, the defendant, Xiamen United Development Company, was not at fault in the process of applying for the establishment of United Development Trade Company and should not, in accordance with the law, assume civil liability for the acts of United Development Trade Company.

In summary, United Development Trade Company was an enterprise legal person approved and registered by the competent authorities and should independently assume civil liability to the outside world in accordance with the law. Xiamen United Development Company and United Development Trade Company were two independent legal entities. The former was not at fault in the process of establishing the latter and should not, in accordance with the law, bear joint and several compensation liability for the debts of United Development Trade Company. The claims of U.S. Minerals were unsupported by evidence and should be dismissed in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 36, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: The claims of U.S. Minerals were dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 320,317.22 was to be borne by U.S. Minerals.

U.S. Minerals, dissatisfied with the judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing:

I. The judgment of the court of first instance made errors in finding the facts.

1. The judgment of the court of first instance found that the respondent "was not at fault in the process of establishing United Development Trade Company," but in fact, the respondent's fault in establishing United Development Trade Company was very obvious. (1) According to the relevant provisions of Chinese laws on three types of foreign-invested enterprises, wholly state-owned enterprises and three types of foreign-invested enterprises are fundamentally different in terms of enterprise nature, the subject of establishment, the source and nature of property, and the conditions for establishment. A three-type foreign-invested enterprise cannot, as the state or on behalf of the state, invest in establishing a wholly state-owned enterprise. Any wholly-owned subsidiary established by it through reinvestment can only be of a three-type foreign-invested enterprise nature. However, the respondent, as a Sino-foreign joint venture, actually established United Development Trade Company as a "wholly state-owned enterprise," which clearly violated Article 37 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which requires that legal persons be "established in accordance with the law." (2) When the respondent applied to the competent authorities for the establishment of United Development Trade Company, it falsely claimed that there was "no foreign equity participation," thereby deceiving the competent authorities into granting approval. This constituted the use of fraudulent means to establish an enterprise and was a serious illegal act. (3) The respondent's violation of relevant Chinese regulations and illegal establishment of United Development Trade Company to engage in import and export trade infringed upon China's foreign trade management system and foreign investment management system. The purpose of the respondent in establishing United Development Trade Company was seriously illegal. (4) The former MOFTEC specifically issued a document in 1998, clearly stating that "according to the current relevant foreign investment regulations of China, Xiamen United Development Company cannot set up an import and export trading subsidiary," and revoked the foreign trade import and export business operation rights of United Development Trade Company. This indicated that the approval document issued by the Xiamen Economic and Trade Commission for the establishment of United Development Trade Company was erroneous, and the respondent had essentially obtained the approval documents from the competent authorities through fraudulent means and subsequently used the approval as an excuse to deny the illegality of its own actions and to evade its responsibilities.

2. The judgment of the court of first instance erroneously found that the respondent "did not have a situation of insufficient registered capital" for United Development Trade Company. In the industrial and commercial registration materials of United Development Trade Company, there were three documents proving the capital contribution status of United Development Trade Company: a "Certificate of Financial Standing" issued by the Xiamen Economic and Trade Commission on June 17, 1986, confirming that the registered capital of United Development Trade Company was RMB 5 million; a "Registered Capital Verification Report" issued by Xiamen Certified Public Accountants on May 9, 1989, proving that the registered capital of United Development Trade Company was RMB 1 million and had been allocated by the respondent as working capital on May 16, 1987; and a letter sent by the Xiamen Finance Bureau to the Xiamen Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce in October 1990, stating that United Development Trade Company had actual capital of RMB 1 million. It can be seen that the description of the source of registered capital of United Development Trade Company was inconsistent and contradictory. It could not be determined based on these three documents that the respondent's registered capital contribution to United Development Trade Company was sufficient. If the respondent could not produce original bank records to verify the contribution, it should be found that the respondent had not actually invested registered capital in United Development Trade Company. Pursuant to the Supreme People's Court's Fa Fu (1994) No. 4 document, the respondent should bear full responsibility for the debt in this case.

II. The judgment of the court of first instance applied the law incorrectly. 1. United Development Trade Company was established illegally and did not meet the conditions for an independent legal person; it could not independently assume responsibility to the outside world. 2. The respondent's act of illegally establishing United Development Trade Company was void ab initio, and the respondent should, in accordance with the law, assume full responsibility to the appellant. 3. The respondent's act of establishing United Development Trade Company for illegal purposes through illegal means violated the public interest and social and economic order of China. The respondent's act of establishing United Development Trade Company was void ab initio, and the respondent should, in accordance with the law, assume full responsibility for the debt in this case.

III. During the appellant's enforcement of the arbitral award, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court entrusted Xiamen Jingxian United Certified Public Accountants to audit the collection of payments for the goods received by United Development Trade Company. The "Special Audit Report" (Xia Xian Hui (2003) Shen Zi No. 01723) issued by the accounting firm on February 11, 2003, showed that United Development Trade Company had recovered most of the payments under the relevant transactions but did not provide any explanation regarding the whereabouts of the recovered payments. The respondent's vice chairman and general manager concurrently served as the legal representative of United Development Trade Company. Thus, the respondent exercised de facto control over United Development Trade Company. Since United Development Trade Company's business license has been revoked, and the respondent cannot provide a reasonable explanation for the whereabouts of the recovered payments, the appellant believes that the recovered payments were illegally transferred by the respondent. In addition, the appellant is currently unable to ascertain whether there were other situations of commingling of property or accounts between the respondent and United Development Trade Company. Therefore, the appellant requests that the court of second instance order a new financial audit of United Development Trade Company. The appellant requests: 1. Reversal of the judgment of the court of first instance; 2. A judgment ordering the respondent to pay the appellant USD 7,495,343.40 plus interest at an annual rate of 8% from February 1, 1996 to the date of actual payment; 3. The respondent to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances, audit costs, and other expenses.

Xiamen United Development Company responded:

I. The establishment of United Development Trade Company complied with legal procedures and it should independently assume civil liability to the outside world in accordance with the law. After the establishment of United Development Trade Company, its business operation rights and subsequent name change were confirmed by the former MOFTEC. The creditor-debtor relationship between the appellant and United Development Trade Company should be enjoyed and borne by those two companies and is irrelevant to any other company. The establishment of United Development Trade Company also did not violate the spirit of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on Issues Regarding Civil Liability After Other Enterprises Established by an Enterprise Are Revoked or Cease Business.

II. Xiamen United Development Company and United Development Trade Company are two independent legal entities. Xiamen United Development Company was not at fault in the process of establishing United Development Trade Company and should not, in accordance with the law, bear joint and several compensation liability for the debts of United Development Trade Company. Moreover, the appellant's assertion that Xiamen United Development Company was at fault is not supported by any evidence. Even if the former MOFTEC revoked the business operation rights of United Development Trade Company, that did not negate the enterprise legal personality of United Development Trade Company. As long as the company has not been legally cancelled, its enterprise legal personality still exists and does not affect its assumption of civil liability. The respondent requests: Dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The appellant, U.S. Minerals, had no substantial objection to the facts found by the court of first instance but only raised objections to the application of the law. Therefore, this Court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

Upon trial, this Court holds:

I. On the issue of the applicable law for this dispute

There is no direct legal relationship between the parties to this case. U.S. Minerals brought this debt dispute lawsuit against Xiamen United Development Company based on the creditor-debt relationship between itself and United Development Trade Company and the fact that United Development Trade Company was established by Xiamen United Development Company. According to the principle of the closest connection in private international law, since Xiamen United Development Company is a Chinese legal person, the law of the People's Republic of China should apply to this debt dispute. Both parties have no objection to this.

II. On whether Xiamen United Development Company should bear joint and several liability for the debt of United Development Trade Company to U.S. Minerals

The debt on which U.S. Minerals based its lawsuit arose from the purchase and sale contracts between itself and United Development Trade Company, and the dispute over those contracts has already been the subject of an arbitral award. There is no direct contractual relationship (creditor-debt relationship) between U.S. Minerals and Xiamen United Development Company. The main reason U.S. Minerals brought this lawsuit is that Xiamen United Development Company illegally established United Development Trade Company.

Article 36(1) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC provides: "A legal person is an organization that has the capacity for civil rights and civil conduct, and independently enjoys civil rights and assumes civil obligations in accordance with the law." Article 3(2) of the Company Law of the PRC provides: "For a limited liability company, shareholders shall bear liability for the company to the extent of their capital contributions, and the company shall bear liability for its debts with all of its assets." The essence of the lawsuit filed by U.S. Minerals Company is to deny the corporate personality of Lianfa Trade Company. The essence of a shareholder's abuse of corporate personality and use of the veil of limited liability to infringe upon the interests of the company and its creditors includes: transferring assets, evading debts, and using those assets to establish a new company; withdrawing capital after the establishment of a new company; commingling company assets with shareholder assets; or arbitrarily interfering in the company's affairs, rendering the company's operational autonomy nominal, among other actions. Under China's corporate registration management system, the scope of application of limited liability is primarily determined through enterprise registration by the administrative department for industry and commerce. Any enterprise registered as a legal person has its founders or investors bearing only limited liability for the enterprise's debts. From the perspective of corporate governance, when the administrative department for industry and commerce registers an enterprise as a legal person, it is unable to conduct a substantive and strict review of whether all enterprises applying for establishment meet the conditions for being a legal person. To prevent the abuse of limited liability, it is insufficient to rely solely on formal requirements; substantive requirements are also necessary. Based on the actual circumstances of this case, the establishment process of Lianfa Trade Company and the changes to its registered capital were both approved by the competent government authorities. U.S. Minerals Company has not adduced evidence to prove the existence of facts that Xiamen Lianfa Company transferred assets with the intent to maliciously evade debts, nor has it adduced evidence to prove the existence of facts that Xiamen Lianfa Company withdrew capital. Furthermore, U.S. Minerals Company engaged in trade transactions with Lianfa Trade Company six years after Lianfa Trade Company was established. Therefore, there is no factual basis for denying the corporate personality of Lianfa Trade Company.

Regarding the issue of this Court's Reply No. Fa Fu [1994] 4, "Reply on Issues concerning Civil Liability after Other Enterprises Established by an Enterprise Are Dissolved or Cease Operations," paragraph 1, item 2 of that Reply provides: "If an other enterprise established by an enterprise has obtained a business license for an enterprise legal person, and although the self-owned funds actually invested do not match the registered capital, they have reached the amount specified in Article 15(7) of the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Regulations of the PRC on the Administration of Enterprise Legal Person Registration or the amount specified in other relevant regulations, and the enterprise meets the other conditions for being a legal person, it shall be deemed to have legal person status, and shall independently bear civil liability with its assets. However, if after the enterprise is dissolved or ceases operations, its assets are insufficient to satisfy its debts, the establishing enterprise shall bear civil liability within the scope of the difference between the self-owned funds actually invested and the registered capital." Paragraph 1, item 3 of that Reply provides: "If an other enterprise established by an enterprise has obtained a business license for an enterprise legal person, but has actually invested no self-owned funds, or the self-owned funds actually invested do not reach the amount specified in Article 15(7) of the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Regulations of the PRC on the Administration of Enterprise Legal Person Registration or the amount specified in other relevant regulations, or it does not meet the other conditions for being a legal person, it shall be deemed not to have legal person status, and its civil liability shall be borne by the enterprise legal person that established it." In essence, it is only when the enterprise legal person that established the other enterprise has made insufficient capital contributions or no capital contributions at all that the establishing enterprise legal person bears civil liability within the scope of the capital shortfall or bears full civil liability. The present case does not fall within the circumstances provided for in the above provisions.

As to the issue of U.S. Minerals Company's request for a financial audit of Lianfa Trade Company: U.S. Minerals Company's request, based on its subjective speculation, to conduct a financial audit of Lianfa Trade Company, which is not a party to the dispute in this case, has no factual or legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, even if there were certain defects in the establishment process of Lianfa Trade Company, U.S. Minerals Company has not provided sufficient evidence to deny the corporate personality of Lianfa Trade Company. U.S. Minerals Company's claim that Xiamen Lianfa Company should bear joint and several liability for the debts of Lianfa Trade Company lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. The facts found in the original judgment are clear, and the judgment result is correct, and it should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby orders as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 320,317.22 shall be borne by U.S. Minerals Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yun

Acting Judge: Chen Jizhong

Acting Judge: Zhou Xiang

January 4, 2005

Court Clerk: Fu Xiaoqiang (substituting)
